name: Enfield

licensing.selective: A new selective licensing scheme started on 1 September 2026 and runs until 31 August 2031. It covers homes let to one or two people or a single family in 17 wards, in two designations: Bowes, Brimsdown, Bullsmoor, Carterhatch, Edmonton Green, Enfield Lock, Haselbury, Jubilee, Lower Edmonton, Ponders End, Southbury, Upper Edmonton and Whitewebbs; and New Southgate, Palmers Green, Southgate and Town. It replaces the earlier 14-ward scheme; licences issued under that scheme stay valid until their own expiry date.
licensing.additional: Borough-wide additional HMO licensing has applied since 1 September 2025, for shared homes with three or four people from two or more households.
licensing.fee: The new selective licence was proposed at £750 (in two parts, with discounts) in the council's scrutiny papers; check the final fee with the council.

housing: Enfield is an outer borough where inter-war semis and Edwardian terraces dominate the west and south, while the east, around Edmonton and Ponders End, has more Victorian terraces split into flats and large post-war council estates. Private renting rose sharply between the 2011 and 2021 censuses, to more than a quarter of households. Big regeneration schemes, such as Meridian Water in Upper Edmonton, are adding new-build flats. The council has widened selective licensing to 17 wards from September 2026 and licenses smaller HMOs borough-wide.
checkinTips: Edwardian and Victorian terraces converted into flats: photograph the shared hallway, the meter cupboard and any fire doors, and record which keys open the communal front door.
Inter-war semis with original or replaced bay windows: photograph each window's locks, seals and any condensation marks on the sills.
Front and back gardens on family houses: photograph the lawn, fences, gates and any shed, as the garden's condition is a common check-out dispute.
Council and housing association blocks in Edmonton and Ponders End: note the fob count, the bin store and any lift or entry-phone faults on the day.
New-build flats at Meridian Water and other developments: photograph the sealed worktops, flooring joints and any snagging marks so they aren't charged later.
Older terraces with suspended timber floors: check skirting boards and corners for damp or mould and photograph them close up.
tenantHelp: Private tenants with disrepair, damp or safety problems can contact Enfield Council's private sector housing team, which can inspect and take action against landlords under the Housing Act 2004.
